title: SELECT, columns, DISTINCT
explanation: SQL is how you ask a database for data. Every question starts with SELECT, which means 'show me', followed by the columns you want. Then FROM says which table to look in. To get every column, use * (a star means 'everything'). And DISTINCT removes repeats, so each value shows only once.

lines.explain: Show me the title and genre columns. Commas separate the columns.
Look inside the games table. The semicolon means 'I'm done'.

tasks.prompt: Show the title of every game.
hints: You only need one column. Which one has the game names?
Start with SELECT title, then say which table it's FROM.

tasks.prompt: Show the title and price of every game.
hints: You need two columns this time.
Put a comma between title and price.

solution_lines.explain: Show me two columns, separated by a comma.

tasks.prompt: Show every column in the games table.
hints: There's a shortcut so you don't have to type every column name.

solution_lines.explain: The star means show me every column.

tasks.prompt: Show each genre only once, with no repeats.
hints: Without help, genres like Shooter would show up more than once.

solution_lines.explain: Show me the genre column, but remove repeats.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: how many rows will this return? SELECT DISTINCT release_year FROM games;
hints: Some games came out in the same year.
Count each year only once. 2017 has four games but counts as one.

solution_lines.explain: Show each release year once, removing repeats.

recap: You just learned to pick columns with SELECT, get everything with *, and remove repeats with DISTINCT.
